questions.stem: Which blood group is considered a universal donor?
questions.solution: Blood group O is considered a universal donor because it lacks both A and B antigens, allowing it to be safely given to individuals with any blood type. AB blood contains both antigens and cannot be given to others without causing a reaction. A and B blood have one antigen each, limiting their compatibility with only certain blood types.

hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses standard Hindi terminology for blood groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of blood?
questions.solution: Blood is responsible for transporting gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide throughout the body, which is a key function of the circulatory system. Producing oxygen is not a function of blood, as oxygen is absorbed from the lungs. Forming urine is the role of the kidneys, not blood. Regulating body temperature is primarily managed by mechanisms like sweating and blood flow to the skin, not directly by blood itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following is responsible for carrying oxygen in the blood?
questions.solution: Red blood cells are responsible for carrying oxygen in the blood because they contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds to oxygen molecules. Plasma is the liquid part of blood and does not carry oxygen. White blood cells are involved in the immune response, and platelets are used for blood clotting, not oxygen transport.

questions.stem: A person with blood group O is called a universal donor because their blood lacks which component?
questions.solution: Blood group O is considered a universal donor because it lacks antigens, which are the substances that can trigger immune responses in recipients. Antibodies are present in all blood types and are not the reason for compatibility. Plasma and platelets are components of blood but do not determine compatibility in the same way antigens do.

questions.stem: If a person has a blood group of AB and is a universal recipient, which of the following is true?
choices: They can receive blood from all groups
They can donate blood to all groups
They can only receive blood from AB
They can only donate blood to AB
questions.solution: AB blood type is known as the universal recipient because it can accept blood from all other blood groups. This is due to the presence of both A and B antigens on red blood cells, which do not trigger an immune response when receiving blood from other types. However, AB individuals can only donate blood to other AB individuals because their blood contains both antigens. Therefore, the statement that they can receive blood from all groups is correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about capillaries?

They allow exchange of materials with cells
questions.solution: Capillaries allow exchange of materials with cells because their walls are extremely thin, consisting of a single layer of cells, which facilitates the diffusion of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products. They do not have thick walls, as that would hinder exchange. Capillaries are not the largest blood vessels, and they do not exclusively carry oxygenated blood, as some carry deoxygenated blood.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why the walls of the lungs are elastic?

mr.solution: योग्य उत्तर हे बालकांचा उच्च विकासक क्रियाशीलता असते. उच्च विकासक क्रियाशीलता शरीराला अधिक ऑक्सीजन आणि पोषक घटक देण्याची आवश्यकता असते, जे उच्च हृदयाच्या धडधडीद्वारे पूर्ण केले जाते. इतर विकल्प चुकीचे आहेत कारण हृदयाच्या आकार, रक्ताची जास्त पातळपणा आणि रक्तवाहिन्यांची संख्या हा संदर्भात हृदयाच्या धडधडीला थोडे नियंत्रित करत नाहीत.
